content.title: About
content.content: Biscuit with fruit is a sweet baked treat that incorporates pieces of dried fruit (raisins, apricots, cranberries, etc.) into the dough. It features a crisp edge and a soft, aromatic interior, combining the buttery flavor of the biscuit with the natural sweetness of the fruit.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipes for fruit biscuits appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a way to use surplus dried fruit.
Dried fruit in biscuits retains a large portion of vitamins and minerals, especially vitamin C and potassium.
Traditionally, fruit biscuits were baked in home ovens, but today they are widely available in stores and cafés.
Different cultures use different fruit mixes: in England raisins and candied peel are common, while in Scandinavia cranberries and prunes are favored.
Fruit biscuits are often served with tea or coffee, as their sweetness balances the bitterness of the drinks.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dried fruits provide dietary fiber that supports regular bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Fruits such as cranberries and raisins are rich in polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Simple sugars in dried fruit are quickly absorbed, giving a rapid energy lift, making the biscuit a convenient snack.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fruit biscuits contain potassium, iron and vitamin K, which contribute to heart and bone health.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: The biscuit dough is typically made with butter, providing essential fatty acids when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Both the dried fruit and added sugar make the biscuit calorie‑dense; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Additive presence
items.content: Some commercial versions may contain preservatives and artificial flavors that are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Risk of overconsumption
items.content: The crunchy texture and sweet taste can lead to eating larger amounts than intended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fruit biscuits can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to yogurt or granola, or used as a base for dessert plates. They are also convenient to pack for hikes and trips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store biscuits in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent mold growth.
